title: Low-poly prop (UltraTex pipeline)
description: Weapons, furniture, pickups, scenery. About 3,000 triangles with a baked normal map and 2K PBR textures. Tuned and verified on a 16 GB card. Slower (about 4-5 min) and its texture weights are reported non-commercial; the default on cards under 12 GB.

param_help.tris: triangle budget of the final mesh
param_help.thin: 0.0-1.0, thickens thin parts before clean-up; raise to 0.8-0.9 for poles, blades, chains
param_help.voxel_size: low-poly rebuild grid; 0.0015 shatters thin props, 0.005 is safe
param_help.trellis: true = TRELLIS.2 (upright, true 3D); false = Pixal3D (follows the picture's camera, can flatten or tilt)
param_help.highpoly_faces: size of the high-poly mesh the normal map is baked from (trimmed on the GPU)
param_help.shape_resolution: voxel resolution of the high-poly shape: 1024 or 1536. Measured on one prop: 1536 took 810 s, 1024 took 322 s, with no visible difference at 3,000 triangles
param_help.quad_resolution: 512 / 1024 / 1536; 1536 runs out of memory on 16 GB
param_help.components: keep_all keeps separate parts; largest drops everything but the biggest piece
param_help.wtivo_resolution: grid of the watertight rebuild: 1024 is about twice as fast as 1536
param_help.albedo_views: colour views painted by the texture model: 6, 10 or 12
param_help.texture_steps: sampling steps of the texture model (UltraTex on FLUX.2 Klein base). Its own guidance is 25; 4 is a preview and loses surface detail. Time grows in proportion
param_help.structure_steps: sampling steps of the three shape stages (structure / shape / upsample)

fast.description: Quickest usable result at the lowest triangle count: coarser grids, fewer sampling steps, fewer texture views.

max.description: Highest quality in one piece: full shape resolution, 8,000 triangles, texture sampling at the texture model's recommended 25 steps.
